title: Engineering foundations, FPA, AIPE, and Staff scope
description: Phase: F0 — Accelerator Platform. Prior status: Not started, according to program progress. Longitudinal system: P0 — initialization of the real repository, apps/portfolio/, and the bilingual site/. This session prepares them conceptually; implementation belongs to Build, after studying and discussing the theory.

sections.title: Objective
paragraphs: Build an initial model for reasoning about software at different levels, from components to systems and platforms. Use that model to understand how architecture, quality attributes, system boundaries, the frontend platform, products with artificial intelligence, and Staff and Principal scope relate to one another.
The goal is not to diagnose your competencies through an interview. Learning evidence will be gathered gradually while studying, designing, building, and operating the program’s systems.

sections.title: Learning Preview
paragraphs: By the end of the theory, you will be able to explain how software engineering and architecture relate; what distinguishes an application, system, platform, and ecosystem; why requirements such as security, performance, and ease of change influence architecture; how boundaries and dependencies affect change; what Frontend Platform Architecture (FPA) covers; how AI Product Engineering (AIPE) connects artificial intelligence models with products and their risks; and how to expand reasoning from delivering a component to impact across teams and organizations.

sections.title: Concepts — Pre-training
paragraphs: These eight concepts establish the vocabulary for the session. The definitions of FPA, AIPE, and professional scope are operational definitions for this learning path; they are not presented as universal taxonomies.

sections.title: 1 — Software engineering and architecture
paragraphs: Software engineering covers the disciplined work of understanding needs and designing, building, verifying, deploying, operating, and evolving software. The IEEE Computer Society’s Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK) organizes areas such as requirements, architecture, design, construction, testing, maintenance, quality, and security. [R2]

blocks.text: Architecture concerns structural decisions that influence how a system is organized and whether it can achieve its objectives under given constraints. Architecture is not identical to its diagram or document: standard 42010 from the International Organization for Standardization, International Electrotechnical Commission, and Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (ISO/IEC/IEEE) distinguishes the architecture of an entity from the description that represents it. [R1]

Software engineering includes implementing a form as well as checking, deploying, and maintaining it. An architectural decision would be determining whether that form’s validation lives in the browser, on the server, or in both.

diagram.title: Relationship among description, architecture, quality, and evidence
diagram.description: Context defines the quality attribute; it influences architectural decisions and observable behavior. A description communicates the architecture and guides evidence, but does not prove quality by itself.

sections.title: 2 — Application, system, platform, and ecosystem
paragraphs: These are related levels of scope, but they are not synonyms.
Application: software that provides capabilities to users or processes. A web portfolio is an application.
System: a coordinated set of software, data, infrastructure, and people that works together to fulfill a mission. An application may be only one part.

Platform: reusable capabilities and contracts that enable multiple products or teams to build and operate applications. A design system with components, tokens, and accessibility rules can be a frontend platform.
Ecosystem: the broader set of organizations, products, integrations, rules, and users that interact around a platform or domain.

Important distinction: a shared library does not automatically become a platform. To call it a platform in the sense used by this course, it must provide reusable capabilities with interfaces and adoption conditions that its consumers can understand.

sections.title: 3 — Quality attributes and constraints
paragraphs: A quality attribute describes a property of the system’s behavior or evolution, such as performance, security, availability, usability, or modifiability. A constraint limits the available options; it can come from the business, regulatory requirements, technical compatibility, budget, or team capabilities.

blocks.text: If a feature must remain available when an external service fails, the design must specify how it will detect the failure and what response it will give the user. Carnegie Mellon’s Software Engineering Institute (SEI) explains that quality-attribute requirements significantly influence architecture and recommends making them specific through scenarios. [R3]

A list of words such as “fast, secure, and scalable” does not by itself define a verifiable goal. A useful scenario identifies who or what initiates an action, under what condition it occurs, what outcome is expected, and how that outcome will be observed.

sections.title: 4 — Boundaries
paragraphs: A boundary establishes which responsibilities, data, or decisions belong to a software element and which remain outside it. A boundary can exist between two modules, between browser and server, between an application and a platform, or between a product and an external provider.

blocks.text: Boundaries become visible through interfaces, data schemas, permissions, protocols, and operating agreements. If a component must directly access the internal data of many other components, the boundary may exist in the diagram but may not be respected in the implementation.

sections.title: 5 — Coupling and cohesion
paragraphs: Coupling describes how much a component depends on the details or decisions of other components. Cohesion describes how closely related the responsibilities grouped within a component are.

blocks.text: As a design heuristic, a system is often easier to change when its boundaries reduce unnecessary dependencies and each component retains coherent responsibilities. This is not a law that “less coupling is always better”: dividing a system also adds contracts, coordination, and operational costs.
If the profile module imports the internal structure of the billing database, a billing change may force a profile change. If both agree on a stable contract, that dependency can be reduced.

sections.title: 6 — FPA: frontend platform architecture
paragraphs: In this program, Frontend Platform Architecture (FPA) means designing and evolving frontend capabilities that are reusable by different applications or teams: design systems, visual tokens, components, internationalization, accessibility, navigation, build tooling, frontend observability, and developer experience.

blocks.text: This is an operational definition for the learning path, not a universal normative definition. The goal of a frontend platform is not to centralize every visual decision; it is to facilitate shared solutions without hiding legitimate product needs.

sections.title: 7 — AIPE: AI product engineering
paragraphs: In this program, AI Product Engineering (AIPE) means integrating artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities into software products so that their inputs, outputs, boundaries, risks, and evaluation mechanisms are part of the product design.

blocks.text: An AI product is not defined only by the model it calls. User experience, data, the tools the model can use, human review when appropriate, security, and how incorrect answers are detected also matter. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) voluntary AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) organizes trustworthiness considerations for the design, development, use, and evaluation of AI products and systems. NIST states that AI RMF 1.0 is under review, so it should be consulted as current guidance subject to change, not as an immutable rule. [R4]

sections.title: 8 — Staff and Principal scope
paragraphs: In this learning path, Staff reasoning focuses on delivering and operating systems, solving problems that cross components or teams, explaining decisions, and managing the consequences of change.

Principal reasoning extends that scope toward shared capabilities, standards, exceptions, technical strategy, and adoption across multiple teams. This distinction is a pedagogical framework for the program, not a universal definition of titles: actual scope varies across organizations.

blocks.text: If a decision improves one module but makes the whole product harder, at what level should you expand the analysis?
blocks.answer: At least to the system that experiences the consequence; if the impact reaches shared capabilities or multiple teams, expand the analysis to the platform or organization.

sections.title: Main Topic — Engineering foundations: deciding with a system model
paragraphs: Software engineering turns needs into systems that can be built, verified, and maintained. Architecture organizes structural decisions within that work. To make useful decisions, an engineer needs to know which system is under consideration, which properties matter, where its boundaries lie, and who will experience the consequences.

blocks.text: Why is it not enough to say that the application must be “secure and fast”?

Consider an application that receives documents and helps a person review them. The application is one part of the system. An application programming interface (API), a database, document storage, an artificial intelligence provider, access controls, human review processes, and support mechanisms might also participate. If documents pass through external systems, those integrations also influence security, availability, and cost.

Architectural decisions connect needs with mechanisms. If the interface must support multiple languages, the content structure and routes must allow language selection without duplicating every function. If document exposure must be limited, authorization and data-access boundaries must match that need. If the interface is expected to change often, separation of responsibilities may reduce the cost of some changes; maintaining that separation also requires work and coordination.

Architecture is therefore not evaluated only by its shape. It is evaluated according to context and the consequences of its decisions. The SEI notes that quality-attribute scenarios help make requirements precise and support reasoning about how patterns and components may contribute to them. [R3]
Initial model: need and context → properties and constraints that matter → boundaries, responsibilities, and contracts → components and their dependencies → observable behavior and consequences.
Which steps connect context to consequences?
blocks.answer: Context → needs and constraints → boundaries and contracts → components and dependencies → observable behavior and consequences. The model guides questions; it does not guarantee outcomes.

blocks.text: This model does not replace detailed analysis or guarantee that the system will meet its objectives. It helps identify what must be checked and which decision may affect the outcome. An architecture document can communicate that decision, but it is not the architecture itself; ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 explicitly distinguishes the entity from its description. [R1]

Because those words do not by themselves identify a verifiable condition, a specific threat or load, or the outcome that must be observed. The team needs to make them concrete through scenarios appropriate to the system and review which decisions contribute to satisfying them.

sections.title: Subtopics
paragraphs: The following seven subtopics develop the central model through scope, mechanisms, examples, limitations, and production consequences.

sections.title: Software engineering versus architecture
paragraphs: Engineering and architecture are related, but they do not describe the same scope of work.

blocks.text: Is architecture a document?

Software engineering covers multiple lifecycle activities. Architecture concentrates on structural decisions and their effects on the system. ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 addresses requirements for expressing architecture descriptions of entities as varied as software, systems, enterprises, and products; it does not prescribe a single notation or working process. [R1]

A structural decision distributes responsibilities, establishes relationships, or defines constraints. For example, deciding that the browser never stores an access secret changes where some operations run and which interfaces the server requires.

“Use a blue button” may be a local visual decision. “All action buttons use a shared component that applies accessible roles and brand styles” may be part of a platform decision. The scope of a decision depends on its consumers and effects, not on the length of its description.

Explain decisions in terms of the need they address, their alternatives, and their consequences. A diagram may help communicate them, but it does not by itself demonstrate that the system meets performance, security, or accessibility goals.
No. Architecture belongs to the designed entity; a document or diagram is a description that communicates it. ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 distinguishes the two. [R1]

sections.title: Application, system, platform, and ecosystem
paragraphs: These terms describe different scales of capability and interaction.

blocks.text: How do application, system, and platform differ?

Standard 42010 considers entities of interest at different levels and separates each entity from its architecture description; the earlier classification is a teaching model for the learning path, not a taxonomy required by the standard. [R1]

An application consumes capabilities; a system coordinates elements to fulfill a mission; a platform publishes reusable capabilities through contracts; an ecosystem includes other products, participants, and interaction rules.

The program’s learning site would be an application. The repository, its publication process, its content, and its users form aspects of a system. Reusable interface components, styles, navigation, and accessible functions could constitute platform capabilities if they are designed for multiple consumers.

Turning a local solution into a platform too early can impose unjustified abstractions and governance. Keeping everything local, on the other hand, can duplicate maintenance when multiple applications truly share a need.
An application provides capabilities; a system coordinates elements for a mission; a platform provides reusable capabilities to consumers. An ecosystem includes broader participants and interactions.

sections.title: Quality attributes and constraints
paragraphs: Attributes express important system properties; constraints narrow the set of valid solutions.

blocks.text: Why is “fast and secure” insufficient as an architectural requirement?
They are not entirely separate categories: a required level of protection or compatibility can function as both a requirement and a design limit.

A quality need influences components, contracts, technologies, and operations. Security may require server-side authorization controls; modifiability may favor boundaries between responsibilities; availability may require recovery procedures. The SEI describes how attributes such as performance, security, modifiability, reliability, and usability affect architecture. [R3]

Worked example. Vague requirement: “the AI summary must respond quickly.” Initial rewrite: “when a person requests a summary, the interface shows that processing is under way and delivers either a result or a controlled error message.” Concrete measures remain open, including the target time and behavior during an interruption; they must not be invented without knowing the product needs.
What is missing from “the summary must be fast”?
blocks.answer: A concrete condition, an expected response, and an observable criterion. The exact values depend on the product; none have been specified here.

blocks.text: “We use microservices for scalability” does not prove that a scale need exists or that the decision satisfies it. Each separated service also introduces network calls, partial failures, and distributed operations.
It does not yet express an observable condition or an expected outcome. It must be made concrete through scenarios that fit the context.

sections.title: Boundaries, coupling, and cohesion
paragraphs: Boundaries group responsibilities and define what may depend on what.

blocks.text: Does less coupling mean that components never communicate?
Coupling describes dependencies between components; cohesion describes the relationship among responsibilities within a component.

If one component knows another component’s internal details, a change can propagate across the boundary. If the contract hides those details and contains the necessary information, some changes can remain local. But if the contract is incomplete or unstable, the boundary is only apparent.

A DocumentReview component can request a summary through a SummarizeDocument contract. If it depends on a stable interface, the AI provider might change without forcing a rewrite of the screen. The contract does not solve every change by itself: if the meaning or guarantees of the summary change, the experience and tests may also need to change.
If a frontend component imports the internal storage schema, what risk appears?
blocks.answer: The persistence detail crosses the boundary into the frontend; an internal change can require consumer changes and increases coupling.

blocks.text: Common misinterpretation: “low coupling means components never communicate.” Components collaborate in a functioning system. The question is whether the relationship is explicit, stable, and proportionate to the need.
No. It means reducing unnecessary dependencies and making the dependencies that do exist explicit. Separation also has costs.

sections.title: Frontend Platform Architecture (FPA)
paragraphs: FPA designs common frontend capabilities for multiple products.

blocks.text: What does a frontend platform seek to do?

It includes components, styles, tokens, internationalization, navigation, accessibility, development tools, and publication practices. This session uses it as a working definition for the learning path.

A shared capability establishes an interface through which consumer teams use common behavior. For example, a navigation component might provide semantic structure, keyboard interaction, and a consistent appearance while allowing each product to supply its own destinations.

A shared design system can reduce duplication and make consistency easier, but it can obstruct specific needs when its evolution process is slow or too rigid. An exception may be appropriate when it has an explicit reason and its maintenance cost is evaluated.

Staff can demonstrate that a capability solves a concrete problem for multiple products; Principal can consider adoption, governance, migration, exceptions, and who will be responsible for maintaining it. This is the learning path’s pedagogical framing, not a rule about professional hierarchy.
It seeks to share useful capabilities across products—for example, components, tokens, accessibility, and tools—through understandable contracts and adoption conditions.

sections.title: AI Product Engineering (AIPE)
paragraphs: AIPE connects an AI capability with a product experience and objective.

blocks.text: What makes an AI feature product engineering rather than only a model call?
It also considers the capability’s conditions of use and risks. It is not simply sending a prompt to a model.

A feature might receive a document, extract context, request an answer from a model, verify that the output can be shown safely, and present options to review or correct it. Depending on the use, it may also need logging, limits, evaluation, and an alternative path.

To generate a draft explanation, a product might show the text as an editable proposal and make clear which source was used. This is an illustrative design option; its suitability depends on the use, the users, and the consequences of errors. NIST provides a voluntary framework for integrating trustworthiness considerations throughout the design, development, use, and evaluation of AI systems. [R4]

If the response is not supported by the received document, the interface could communicate unjustified certainty. The system needs to evaluate this class of error in the product context and decide how to communicate or handle it; the mere presence of a model does not prove trustworthiness.
Its integration with the objective, data, experience, risks, evaluations, and behavior under error.

sections.title: Staff and Principal: expanding the unit of reasoning
paragraphs: This learning path uses Staff and Principal as increasing levels of technical and organizational scope.

blocks.text: What changes when reasoning expands from Staff to Principal in this learning path?
They are development objectives for the program, not guaranteed equivalents to titles at a company.

Reasoning expands from code and components to modules, applications, systems, platforms, multiple teams, and strategy. Each expansion introduces new stakeholders, constraints, coordination costs, and consequences of a decision.

To fix inaccessible navigation, a component-level solution can correct the defect on one page. A broader analysis can examine the shared component, consuming products, tests, and the process used to prevent regressions.

Expanding scope without evidence can create bureaucracy and premature decisions. Keeping the view too local can hide shared problems. The scale of analysis should correspond to the probable reach of the impact.
Scope can move from systems and teams to shared capabilities, adoption, governance, and strategy. Actual titles vary by organization.

paragraphs: These are possible ways to gather evidence. They do not yet claim that PA-S001 has produced those tests or results.

rows: Specific requirement, scenario, or quality budget
Test, measurement, review, or observable criterion
Review of changes, API, and tests
Evaluations, failure handling, and a reviewable experience

sections.title: Time Breakdown
paragraphs: Estimated time for this session: 120 minutes. This is a suggested study allocation; it is not based on prior measurements.

sections.title: Real-World Example
paragraphs: NIST publishes the AI RMF as a voluntary framework for incorporating trustworthiness considerations into the design, development, use, and evaluation of AI products, services, and systems. The official page also states that AI RMF 1.0 is under review. This case shows how the design of an AI product must consider its context and lifecycle; it does not demonstrate that adopting a framework, by itself, guarantees a safe or suitable product. [R4]

As another example of architectural guidance, Microsoft documents its Azure Well-Architected Framework as a set of quality-guided principles and tools for analyzing workloads. Its pillars include reliability, security, cost optimization, operational excellence, and performance efficiency. It is a Microsoft framework for its workloads; it serves as an example of analysis, not as a mandatory universal list. [R5]

sections.title: Production-Ready Example
paragraphs: Hypothetical example: a document-review product lets a person request an AI-assisted summary. It does not represent a Thomson Reuters system or describe that company’s internal data or components.

The interface initiates the request and shows its state. The review service verifies permissions, obtains the authorized document, and requests the summary. The provider may respond, take too long, or fail. The product must define what the person sees in each case and what information it retains.

The decisions depend on requirements that remain to be established: which documents each role may process, how long an acceptable response takes, what must be recorded, and what consequences an incorrect summary would have. Diagrams and contracts help review those decisions; they do not replace tests or evaluations.

One important boundary separates authorized access to the document from the AI provider’s capability. Another separates presenting the response from generating it. Those boundaries might make replacing a provider easier, but they also add contracts and error handling.

Illustrative failure: if the provider takes too long, the interface must not remain indefinitely in a loading state. The team must agree on a time limit, an understandable response, and whether the person can retry or complete the task without the summary. Without requirements and tests, no specific architecture can be claimed to be sufficiently reliable.

diagram.title: Hypothetical document-review flow
diagram.description: A reviewer requests a summary in the web interface; the review service coordinates authorized document storage, an AI provider, and an activity log, then returns an editable result with review context.

sections.title: Exercises
paragraphs: The identifiers are written so that study state remains the same in Spanish and English. Checking a box means studied; it does not demonstrate mastery. Recall with answer: if a frontend component imports the internal storage schema, what risk appears? Answer: the persistence detail crosses the boundary into the frontend; an internal change can require consumer changes and increases coupling.

studyItems.label: Classify a website, its API, a shared library, and consuming applications as application, system, platform, or ecosystem. Justify any ambiguous case.
Rewrite “the summary feature must be reliable” as a verifiable scenario. If product information is missing, note what must be obtained.

Describe what the person sees if the AI provider is slow, fails, or returns an unhelpful response. Identify what requires validation with users and product owners.

sections.title: Curated Sources and References
paragraphs: International Organization for Standardization. (2022). ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022 — Software, systems and enterprise — Architecture description. The official record describes the standard’s scope and its distinction between architecture and description. [R1]
IEEE Computer Society. (n.d.). Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK). IEEE describes SWEBOK as an organization of software-engineering processes, models, methods, and practices. [R2]

Software Engineering Institute, Carnegie Mellon University. (2018). Reasoning About Software Quality Attributes. It summarizes how quality-attribute requirements influence architecture and presents scenarios as a way to specify them. [R3]

National Institute of Standards and Technology. (2023–2026). AI Risk Management Framework. A voluntary framework for incorporating trustworthiness considerations; the official page states that AI RMF 1.0 is under review. [R4]
Microsoft. (n.d.). Azure Well-Architected Framework. An example of a quality-guided architecture framework for Azure workloads; its guidance is specific to the context documented by Microsoft. [R5]

sections.title: Resources
paragraphs: For deeper architecture study, review the public record and summary for International Organization for Standardization / International Electrotechnical Commission / Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (ISO/IEC/IEEE) 42010 before consulting the full text, which requires paid access. [R1]

For reasoning about quality, read the Software Engineering Institute (SEI) introduction to modifiability and reliability scenarios. Use its examples as models for writing your own scenarios, not as automatic requirements. [R3]

For AI products, consult the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) and check the date and status of its versions because the framework is under review. [R4]

Initialisms used on this page: phase 0 (F0); project 0 (P0); Principal Accelerator session 001 (PA-S001); Frontend Platform Architecture (FPA); AI Product Engineering (AIPE); artificial intelligence (AI); application programming interface (API); Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK); and mastery levels 1–5 (L1–L5).

sections.title: Knowledge Mastery Checklist
paragraphs: Checking a criterion only records study activity; it does not automatically change the session status or award an L1–L5 level.

studyItems.label: I can explain how software engineering and architecture relate and distinguish architecture from its description.
I can distinguish application, system, platform, and ecosystem and recognize ambiguous cases.
I can turn a vague quality goal into a scenario that identifies what must be observed.
I can identify a boundary and explain how a dependency can propagate a change.
I can explain the purpose and limits of FPA and AIPE under the definitions used by this learning path.
I can explain how analysis changes when moving from component scope to a system, platform, or multiple teams.

sections.title: End-of-Session Success Criteria
paragraphs: These controls record study tracking and appear on the dashboard; they do not claim that the criterion has been demonstrated or change mastery or session status.

studyItems.label: I can explain the context → needs → boundaries → components → consequences model.
I can name an architectural decision and the quality attribute it is intended to address.
I can explain why a diagram, a standard, or a model call does not by itself prove product quality.
I can distinguish an application capability from a platform capability and identify what evidence would clarify the boundary.
I can propose what information is missing before claiming that a quality requirement has been satisfied.

sections.title: Bridge to PA-S002
paragraphs: PA-S001 establishes the language for discussing systems, quality, and boundaries. PA-S002 will use those foundations to study the Accelerator repository as an engineering platform: monorepo versus polyrepo, workspaces, applications and packages, dependency direction, standards, and quality gates.
End of the Theory Phase. The next step is to study and discuss this theory; Design and Build have not yet begun.

modes.label: Change journey
modes.title: How a dependency propagates a modification
modes.rationale: Follows a change from the initial need to observable effects and shows where a contract can contain or transmit it.

steps.title: A need appears
steps.body: A billing rule, the meaning of a summary, or expected timeout behavior changes.

steps.title: The boundary is identified
steps.body: The team locates which module, contract, permission, or provider contains the affected responsibility.

steps.title: The dependency is reviewed
steps.body: If a consumer knows internal details, the change propagates; a stable contract can keep some changes local.

steps.title: The experience is adjusted
steps.body: When meaning or guarantees change, the interface, error handling, and tests may also need to change.

steps.title: The consequence is verified
steps.body: Tests, observation, and review confirm behavior; the diagram alone does not demonstrate it.
